Welcome to Horndean Technology College
Welcome to Horndean Technology College! We wish everyone a safe and pleasant summer. Please be aware HTC is closed over the school holiday. The Headteacher's Letter to Parents can be found on the 'News' section of this website.
Our Curriculum
Find out more about our Curriculum and our extra-curricular offer - 'Curriculum+'
High Performing College
In November 2024, we received an Ofsted Inspection. You can read the full report here!
Values and Ethos
Be Part of our Vision.
Welcome
Learning and student achievement is at the heart of all we do, within and beyond the curriculum. We are committed to achieving excellence for all our students, whether it is in public examinations, on the sports field, in a technology challenge or by taking part in a musical or dance production; the opportunities are extensive. Our curriculum is ‘Outstanding’ (Ofsted), providing students with many choices and different ways of learning.
In addition to this we are fortunate to have a highly dedicated and well qualified staff that teach engaging lessons and support our young people in becoming responsible and successful future citizens. Education is the key to the future: it only happens once in a young person’s life and we make it our duty and responsibility to ensure that it is the best it can be for every student.
An outstanding education for all is our vision and the right of every student. I welcome you to visit the College at any time to witness happy, safe and successful learning.
Mrs J A Summerfield Headteacher
Excellence in Teaching
Find out more about our Curriculum! Our teaching staff and support staff team provide a learning and pastoral environment which allows every student to feel safe, happy and succeed.
Valuing Individuals
At HTC we provide learning which is both challenging and fun! We value every individual and promote the importance of learning which leads to academic success alongside valuable skills for life.
Students
All our students are treated as individuals and learning is delivered to meet their unique needs. They benefit from excellent standards of teaching delivered by qualified and experienced teachers. Technology is a huge part of everyone’s lives so it is important to learn as much about it as possible.
Our College
HTC 2024-2027 Prospectus
Families
Families play a crucial role in their child’s education. We ask that you take an interest, provide facilities and opportunities for students to study at home and ensure they complete their home learning.
Latest News

Further information for students, parents and teachers, can be found on our virtual learning platform at this location: Careers – Horndean Technology College (fireflycloud.net)
THE QUALITY IN CAREERS STANDARD AWARD
HTC is committed to providing outstanding, impartial, independent careers education, information, advice and guidance for all young people. This ongoing commitment has been recognised through the achievement of the Quality in Careers Standard- first awarded in December 2018 and succesfully reaccreditated in June 2025. This is a nationally recognised award and one of the highest accolades a school can receive for excellence in this area and reflects the continued dedication of the Careers Department and the support of its stakeholders.

UNIFROG / WEX
At HTC we work with UNIFROG to provide our students with in-depth career guidance and advice, including a 2 week work experience placement at the end of Year 10. “Unifrog partners with schools to support students to progress into the best opportunity for them. Unifrog does this by providing a one-stop-shop where students can explore their interests, then find and successfully apply for their best next-step after school.”
In collaboration with UNIFROG, HTC provides every student with access to a range of career tools on the Unifrog online platform, where they learn what options are available, access good quality information, and search for opportunities to support their future education and training. Parents are also provided with a login to this online resource.
Our WEX programme is introduced and details outlined to our Year 10 students in an assembly during the Autumn Term and to our Year 10 parents in a bespoke information evening which is included in our College calendar.

Welcome – ‘What Parents Say About Us’
We welcome feedback from parents/carers of existing students and prospective families at all times. If you would like to provide feedback or comments to us please do email us at: general@horndeantc.hants.sch.uk
L White
“I just wanted to thank you for the Tour of the school yesterday morning and to especially extend our thanks to our guide. She was excellent, incredibly polite and very informative. Any questions we asked which she was unable to answer she found out for us from members of staff we met on our way round. We were very impressed by her attitude. She is a credit to the school and felt this should be recognised and fed back to you”.
Year 10 and 11 Parent
“I would like to thank you for the huge support you and your teaching staff provide at HTC. Please can you pass on my gratitude to her respective Teachers for all they have done to help our daughter achieve her grades. She is looking forward to Year 11 with a massive confidence boost, of which I’m sure will help in her studies. Again thank you for making in my opinion Horndean Technology College the best for learning and achieving in Hampshire”.
Open Evening Feedback 2023
“I just wanted to say a huge thank you for putting on such a brilliant Open Evening last night. It was amazing to have the freedom to wander around with our children and access all the amazing activities on offer. Whether it was driving the RC cars, watching some dancing and acting, listening to the steel pan, sampling some delicious sweet treats or just generally getting involved in all the other creative activities and quizzes on offer, it really was a fabulous example of what your school has to offer. My youngest has only just started Year 3 and thoroughly enjoyed last night and is already asking when he can attend another one!”
Year 5 Family Feedback 2023
“My wife and I attended your Open Evening yesterday evening as we’re looking at local secondary schools/colleges for our son Henry who is currently in Year 5. We were really impressed with the campus, facilities and all the opportunities available to students. We also really liked the fact there seemed to be real engagement between the teachers and students. We’d heard lots of positive feedback prior to our visit and left feeling HTC lived up to its reputation of being an engaging, friendly and supportive environment for students to learn and achieve in. That said, the reason for my email is just to make a special mention of the student who showed us round – Oscar.
Oscar was an excellent tour guide – friendly, well spoken, answered all our questions and had a good knowledge of the school. He engaged with our son really well (so much so Henry said he wants to attend HTC so he can see Oscar again) and, out of all of the student guides we’ve had when visiting other local schools, seemed the most confident and outgoing. Oscar really proved to be a great ambassador for HTC so we felt it important to highlight this, so he can be recognised in some way. Please pass on our thanks to Oscar again”.
“As a family we all really love HTC, so hopefully our son will get in, in 2025 as we live outside catchment……..The opportunities sound brilliant. Thank you all so much for answering our questions. The Transition Lead Miss Whiteman was brilliant on our tour yesterday. I loved the way she encouraged the children to project their voices and speak with us all. They all did amazing. Thanks so much – I look forward to our son coming to HTC hopefully if he gets in, in Sept 2025”.
Family Feedback on our Student Tour Guides 2023/2024
“I particularly wanted to mention a wonderfully talented young man called Jenson in Year 8. We came across him playing some funky tunes on the bass guitar in Music and although he wasn’t an official Tour Guide, he was extremely knowledgeable and amazing at informing us of all the opportunities that HTC has to offer and gave us a thorough insight into his own personal experience of being a pupil at HTC. He then, of his own accord, offered to show us around at some of the other departments that we were keen to see.
I would be really appreciative if you could pass on our thanks to him, and even his parents if possible, as he really did go above and beyond… He was a remarkable young man that really impressed us: polite, confident, patient and extremely accommodating and we were very grateful of his support last night. We look forward to coming to see your production of ‘Little House of Horrors’ and hearing him strum his stuff on the bass guitar again”.
Year 4/5 Open Morning Tour Feedback
“The tour was very well organised and the student guides in Group 4 were very knowledgeable and confident. Eden cannot wait to start!” Parent/Carer
“Our Tour Guides were really interested and positive. In classes, the behaviour was outstanding….” – Parent/Carer
“Very impressed with the behaviour of the students in all the classes and the teachers were very welcoming. Everyone taking us round both students and adults were very informative and the students were clearly proud of their school.” – Parent/Carer
Year 5/6 Tour Feedback
“I enjoyed coming back to see the school with my daughter. Lot’s has changed and in a positive way. A good school!” – Ex-Student and Parent
“A very well organised tour with students knowledgeable and well mannered. Hopefully our third daughter will get to attend here!” – Returning Parent
“It (the tour) was a useful insight into the daily workings of secondary school, making the forthcoming transition less daunting” – Parent/Carer
“My daughter really enjoyed looking around and seeing the school in action. Our Tour Guide Megan, was very friendly and informative and Mrs Massink (Year Leader) answered our questions too. We were very impressed, thank you!” – Parent
“A wonderful insightful visit. Impressed with the facilities available to students and the enthusiasm of the Teachers we met. A big thank you to our wonderful Tour Guides who were funny and informative. A great asset to the school!” – Parent
“What a fantastic tour and a really good insight into day-to-day school life. Our Guides, Reid and Evan were excellent. Polite, knowledgeable and friendly. They answered our questions honestly too which really helped us. Thank you!” – Parent/Carer
“The tour was a delight. Your Tour Guides were confident and the feel was friendly throughout. Teachers were all friendly and welcoming. A great morning.” – Parent/Carer

My parents came with us to watch; what an incredible music/arts department we have at HTC. Thanks, to you all, for organising a great evening and giving this opportunity to our children.
Simon Beken
Thank you to all at Horndean Technology College for the learning environment that has delivered a very happy son of ours in the last week. We are, of course, very pleased for him as well!

Safeguarding Young People in Education
Everyone in the Education Service shares an objective to help keep children and young people safe by contributing to providing a safe environment for children and young people to learn, identifying children and young people who are suffering or likely to suffer significant harm, and taking appropriate action with the aim of making sure children are kept safe both at home and in the education setting.
Safeguarding is what we do every day and is everybody’s responsibility. Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is defined as:
At HTC, Mrs Attwood is our Designated Safeguarding Lead who is supported by other specially trained staff known as Deputy DSL’s: Mrs J Skeet, Mrs V Newman and Mrs F Wynn. Mrs N Bugden (Vice Principal of Business and Community) is a Deputy DSL for staff allegations alongside Mrs Attwood. We have trained safeguarding staff in our Childcare Dimension plus Year Leader Mrs Headland, SEN Support Worker Mrs E Reid, Assistant Headteacher Mrs A Marks and Teacher of PE, Mr M Shaw. All staff regularly attend safeguarding and child protection awareness training.

Curriculum +
Curriculum +
The College is proud to offer a diverse and exciting range of extra-curricular activities for students to take part in. These range from Chess Club, Eco Club, DIY and Coursework support as well as Music, Arts and Sporting Clubs.
Our Extra-Curricular programme is called ‘Curriculum Plus’.
Each term there is a Curriculum Plus booklet published of the available activities which is given to each tutor group and also available from Barton Hall Reception. If you are looking for information on our Student Voice, please click here.
In September, there is an Extra-Curricular Fayre in Barton Hall where students and parents can see what activities are on offer and speak to staff and students involved. Students are provided with a card which they can scan, which links to the latest club listings, online.
Last year we performed Shrek the Musical before sell-out audiences. Our previous shows include The Addams Family which was performed here in 2019, and in 2023 we will be performing the HTC production of The Little Shop of Horrors!
The latest Curriculum Plus programme is published to students and their families on our Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) and FireFly.
Just some of our clubs and activities!
Music Tuition
At Horndean Technology College Music and the Performing Arts are a passion!
We will soon be making plans for instrumental/vocal lessons for the next academic year, 2024/2025. If your child is due to be a new student and would like to begin lessons on an instrument or singing, a letter and enrolment form will be available in the Year 6 Admissions’ Pack sent out to you in March 2024. We will then arrange for your child to receive lessons starting in September 2024.
If you are an existing student wishing to sign up for lessons, please speak to Mrs Tanner or Mr Edgell to collect a letter and consent form. These can also be found on Firefly under the Music Tuition page https://htc.fireflycloud.net/extra-curricular/music-tuition-service
The College is fortunate enough to have the specialist skills of 8 instrumental tutors who work as a team to enhance the quality of our music education.
This year we have been able to offer tuition for the following instruments:
*Students in receipt of Free School Meals can receive one group lesson for free, or £50 towards 1:1 lessons.
**Please note that when you are applying for Drum Kit or Piano/Keyboard tuition for your child, the group size will be no more than 2 students.
Should you have any questions about Music Tuition at HTC, please contact Mrs Tanner via email at melanie.tanner@horndeantc.hants.sch.uk.
Breakfast Fitness Club
Fancy a workout before College? Come along and show a great attitude to a healthy lifestyle and we will reward you with a free healthy breakfast token for Cafe X. See Miss Taylor in the PE Office for more information! Open to students in all Year Groups, 7.30-8.00am every Tuesday.
Interactive Gym Club is every Friday 2.10-3.05 with Mrs Whiffin. Students in all Year Groups are welcome.
Greenpower F24 Club
Everyone raves about Greenpower and everyone is welcome to be involved! On a Tuesday after College 2.15-3.30pm, Mr Smith (Teacher of Design Technology) runs our club in W7. Simply put, we design, build, test and race two kit cars which are powered on a car battery. We race against schools from all over the Country at places like Goodwood and Rockingham and had a good track record in National Competitions.
The trick is that as a team, we need to engineer the right combination of lots of different things to get the best distance out of our batteries! Whether you are the brains behind the scenes, an engineer, mechanic or driver we want you to join our team.
We are also always looking for team sponsors and donations to help improve cars and help our team be even more successful. If you know someone who can help, please let us know!
Eco Club - Environmental Awareness
At Horndean Technology College it is important to us that we look after our College environment, to ensure that we maintain our excellent facilities for our community. We recognise that our responsibility towards the environment extends beyond our College grounds and we aim to minimise our environmental impact on both a local and global level.
Students are actively involved in this ongoing process. We have a proactive Eco Club which meets weekly (on Tuesday’s 2.10-3.00pm) to address concerns and ultimately to reduce our impact on the environment. This club is open to students from all year groups, and we have an enthusiastic and dedicated group of students who attend this club regularly.
If you’d like to get involved with our environmental work, speak to your Tutor or Mrs Cutbush in the Science Prep Room for the details of Eco Club!
Tuesday’s 2.10-3.00pm in S5.
Duke of Edinburgh Award
What is the Duke of Edinburgh Award?
The Duke of Edinburgh Award is a registered charity, increasing opportunities for young people between the ages of 14 and 24.
It is a life-changing experience where young people can have fun with friends, discover new interests and talents; as well as developing essential transferable skills for life and employment.
Bronze, Silver and Gold
Young people can participate in a DofE programme at one of three progressively challenging levels: Bronze, Silver and Gold.
There are four sections to complete for both Bronze and Silver level, and five sections to complete at Gold level.
Voluntary Skill Physical Expedition
Gold Voluntary Skill Physical Expedition Residential
Why do the Duke of Edinburgh Award?
The Duke of Edinburgh Award provides a fantastic opportunity for you as a young person to achieve so many things! Not only will you be enhancing your own skills, interests and talents, you will be making friends, helping the community and challenging yourself! You’ll enjoy loads of new experiences as well as having fun along the way! It really is a great opportunity for you, and one you will not want to miss out on!
DofE at HTC
At HTC, you will be supported by a great team of DofE Leaders who you will know and trust. You will have a fantastic support network from staff/leaders and friends who will work tirelessly to ensure you achieve your award. At HTC, you will start your Skills, Physical and Voluntary sections in the Summer term of Year 9 to ensure you have plenty of time to organise your academic work alongside your DofE sections. This has proven to work very well and allows students to organise their time effectively around their studies and personal interests.
Application Process
The Duke of Edinburgh Award is a very popular extra-curricular activity at HTC and therefore we have adopted an application process to ensure all students have an opportunity to express their interest in the award and why they would like to complete it. At HTC we offer the Bronze award to students to complete during Year 10, however we start the application process during the Spring Term of year 9.
Additional information regarding the DofE at HTC can be found on the student firefly page.
We look forward to welcoming you to the Duke of Edinburgh Award.
Miss Taylor – Duke of Edinburgh Award Manager and Co-ordinator

Options
Year 8 Options
In today’s constantly changing society, it is becoming increasingly important for students to develop a range of skills that are transferable and adaptable in the marketplace. HTC has become well known for the outstanding curriculum provision it offers and it is always a challenge to continue to provide this for our students in the ever-evolving world of education in which we live and work. It is our intention to be able to offer a personalised curriculum for all our students so that it continues to be broad, balanced, progressive and relevant to students of all abilities. With this personalised programme it is our intention to provide an experience that stimulates, motivates and extends learners, with a curriculum responsive to their individual interests, needs and aspirations enabling access to more than one learning environment. This will be flexible, enabling learners to combine courses and different types of learning.
Students and parents/carers need to be aware that the Government is constantly reviewing the qualifications recommended for 14-16 students. The nature and timing of this process means that some outcomes will not be known until after students have made their choices. Therefore, it is possible that in some cases, the actual qualifications that students end up sitting may be different from those published on this page. The subjects themselves will remain unchanged, but potentially we may need to amend the qualification students sit. Students and parents will be kept full informed of any relevant developments in this area. It is our aim, that students can take options that satisfy these national requirements but also retain the flexibility which has been so successful in our curriculum in recent years.
Students will choose their options in two groups:
Early Options, Group 1 – Students will select two subjects that will be studied in Years 9 and 10. These subjects will complete their final assessments in Year 10 and will therefore not need to be studied in Year 11. We sometimes refer to these as ‘early entry’ subjects.
General Options, Group 2 – Students will then select five subjects from the Group 2 list. These subjects will be studied in Year 9 and students will then undertake a further options process towards the end of Year 9. At this point, students will select three of these choices which they will then go onto study in Years 10 and 11.
The options you choose could very well determine the career path you follow and your life chances for the future. It is therefore very important that you choose wisely.
Year 8 Options Evening 2024
In order that students can make the most informed choice possible I would encourage them to attend, along with parents, the Year 8 Options Evening on Wednesday 20 March 2024. This evening will begin at 4.30pm. The evening will give students and parents the opportunity to speak with relevant subject specialist staff and Careers professionals as well as see one of the presentations being made by Mr Evans that will cover the options process. The evening will finish by 7.30pm.
For anyone unable to attend on the evening itself, please follow this link to FireFly to view a presentation video by Mr Evans about Year 8 Options.

Year 9 Options
AT HTC we are proud that our curriculum has repeatedly been judged as ‘Outstanding’ and this is clearly a significant contributory factor towards our regularly being placed amongst the top 20% of schools nationally.
Throughout this process, we want all students and parents to be aware of all the national qualification developments that may have an impact on a student’s future opportunities. In particular, you should be aware of Department of Education guidance that recommends the subjects students should study at Key Stage 4. In addition, the Government is constantly in the process of reviewing which qualifications students will be allowed to study. This may mean that while the subjects listed below will not change, the actual qualifications that may be studied are potentially subject to change.
This guidance states that students should take:
One further GCSE from the list below of ‘English Baccalaureate’ subjects:
A minimum of three other high value qualifications which can also include the subjects mentioned above.
(All courses offered at HTC are what the Government describe as ‘high value’).
It is our aim to ensure students are able to access this, while retaining the flexibility which has been so successful in our curriculum in recent years. Therefore, students will be able to choose three option choices for study in Years 10 and 11. These are in addition to the two ‘Early Option’ choices that they are already studying.
You should already be aware that the offer of any option subject is dependent on attitude and performance throughout Year 9 and the advice of the Subject Teacher and/or Subject Leader. In a small number of cases this can lead to a student having limited choices at this stage of the process. If you have any questions about this, please do contact us.
The options you choose could very well determine the career path you follow and your life chances for the future. It is therefore very important that you choose wisely. All students will have been studying two ‘early options’ this year and must now decide which of the five ‘general options’ they have been studying they would like to continue with. In addition to these ‘general options’ students may also be offered a selection of new courses that they do not currently study.

We will do everything we can to meet your requests, but in some cases we are very restricted by the number of rooms, the number of students taking the subject, the amount of specialist equipment or the availability of specialist Teachers. In the event that your first three choices cannot be facilitated then students will be spoken with on an individual basis to discuss the alternatives.
Most of you, in common with students across the country, will continue on to Further Education after Year 11 and the majority will study Level 3 courses. Do remember to plan ahead and therefore consider that courses at local Further Education Colleges often have particular entry criteria and that a vast majority of Level 3 qualifications will require you to attain at least a grade 4 in English and Maths to study that course. Many courses also require Science at the equivalent level. If you do not have a grade 4 in English and Maths then it is likely that you will have to study these subjects again at College until you achieve the required grade.
Making choices is an important part of taking responsibility for ourselves. Ensuring that you work hard for the grades as soon as you start the course will also be beneficial as you approach the final examinations. Please make sure that you ask all the questions you need, gather all of the information possible to ensure that you make an informed decision about your options.

Trips and Visits
HTC organises trips and visits throughout the year which aim to enrich the learning within our broad and diverse curriculum.
As well as the huge programme of sports fixtures which take place as part of friendly and structured leagues and competitions we have taken students on domestic and overseas residentials, team building camps, visits to museums, galleries, live performances and we actively encourage participation in inter-school competitions.
We have an excellent track record in participating and competing against other schools in Business and Enterprise Challenges, Maths Challenges, Tech Days and other showcase events both locally, regionally and nationally. We are always so proud of our students who not only enjoy these events but also gain confidence and develop their leadership skills.
In Autumn 2023 alone, we ran trips to Cobnor Activity Centre, Winchester Science Centre, Woodhorn Farm, Queen Elizabeth Country Park, Havant & South Downs College and Fareham College. During the Spring Term we will be running our annual Year 9 Maths trip to Bletchley Park and the English Department are taking a group of Year 11 students to the King’s Theatre, Southsea to see ‘An Inspector Calls’ in support of their KS4 curriculum.

The Role of the Year Leader:
Our Year Leaders are responsible for the overall personal well-being of your child, including overseeing the progress, attendance and development of students.
The Year Leader alongside the Tutor, is responsible for the support and guidance of each student, and where necessary will liaise with parents, external agencies, and within the College the Learning Support Department, Special Educational Needs Coordinator, and all teaching staff.
The Year Leader will spend time in lessons to help support and guide all students through their learning. Typically, the Year Leader stays with their cohort all the way through the five year learning journey. Year Leaders do morning and afternoon gate duties daily and will be visible in fluorescent jackets.
The Role of the Tutor and how Tutor Time works:
On joining HTC, your child will be placed in one of ten Tutor Groups in the Year Group. If possible, your child’s Tutor will remain the same throughout their five years at HTC.
The Tutor is seen as a very important person as they see your child on a daily basis. Parents are encouraged to contact the Tutor, via the College, if they have a problem concerning their child. Tutors will contact parents/carers if they have any reason to be concerned about a student’s progress or behaviour.
Tutor Groups are block assigned to one of our five Houses, Goodall, Holmes, McKellen, Turing and Windsor. House assemblies are held every half term. Each Tutor base has its own noticeboard where key messages are posted weekly.
Each Tutor Group has two Tutor Captains and in Year 7 these positions are recruited for, and details are circulated to all tutees so that they can choose whether they wish to apply for this initial leadership role.
As a parent, it is important that you contact your child’s Tutor or Student Support Services in the first instance with any issues.
